01 / Less reconstruction. More continuation.
Your work has context.
Keep it close.
When you come back to a project, the first job shouldn’t be remembering what the last job was. Cockpit puts the conversation, the current files and the next decision within reach.
01
Find the thread.
See your recent task, the agent you used, your current branch and changed files. Resume the conversation or start fresh.
02
Make the next call.
See which conversations need you. Approve or deny a command in the thread, then get on with the rest of your work.
03
See what you’re building.
Open your app beside the conversation. Your agent can inspect the preview while you try the result for yourself.
KEEP YOUR TOOLS ↗
Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and OpenCode. Use your installed agents and existing accounts. Switch agents with the transcript as context. Preview tools are available with Claude, Codex and OpenCode.

Download for Mac ↓Release notes ↗SHA-256 ↗
Apple silicon (M1+) · DMG · 133.4 MB
Not notarized. Follow the first-launch steps below.
What you’ll need
  • 01 A Mac with Apple silicon.
    Intel, Windows and Linux aren’t supported.
  • 02 A current Claude Code or Codex CLI, installed and signed in, for the simplest first run.
  • 03 Your own agent access.
    Provider subscriptions and limits still apply.
01 / INSTALL
Install Cockpit.
Open the DMG and drag Cockpit into Applications. Then open Cockpit.
02 / FIRST LAUNCH
Allow the first launch.
If macOS blocks the app, choose Done. Go to System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway, authenticate, then confirm.
03 / PICK UP YOUR WORK
Resume. See the result.
Open a project folder and choose Resume and show me the app. No recent conversation? Explore the project or try the sample. Review the startup approval, then try the preview.


Before you install
A few good
questions.
Does Cockpit include an AI subscription?
No. Cockpit runs the agent CLIs you install and sign into: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and OpenCode (including configured OpenRouter models). Usage is billed or counted by those providers. Cockpit doesn’t supply model access or bypass usage limits.
Where does my work go?
Projects stay in the folders you choose. Cockpit keeps conversation metadata, events and readable Markdown transcripts under ~/.agent-cockpit/ on your Mac. Prompts and attached context go to your selected agent’s provider. There is no Cockpit cloud account or cloud storage.
What should I expect from the prerelease?
v0.1.4 adds find in a conversation, message copying and Mac notifications when an agent finishes or needs you. Check for Updates (since v0.1.3) opens the new installer and you install it yourself. Its Claude compatibility fix passed same-Mac acceptance on a second account in v0.1.2. It isn’t notarized. Independent human and other-Mac installation remain open. Three automated fresh-state runs with a signed-in Claude CLI reached an inspected sample app in 19.9–22.9 seconds; your project and setup may take longer. OpenCode’s live OpenRouter path remains unverified, and Antigravity has no Cockpit preview tools. Read the full release notes before installing.
Can I check in from my phone?
Optional phone access uses your own Tailscale account. Pair your phone to follow conversations, reply, approve requests and stop a turn. Keep your Mac awake and Cockpit running. Physical-phone push notification delivery is not yet verified.
How do workflows run?
Save instructions and agent settings, then run them manually, on an interval, daily, on weekdays, or on selected days at a local time. Cockpit must be running. After downtime, at most one missed run starts when you reopen it; failed runs report their errors and do not block future scheduled runs.
Is this related to Enjoy?
Cockpit is an independent project inspired by Enjoy’s layout and interaction model. It is not affiliated with Enjoy. Cockpit’s code, name, mark and copy are its own; no Enjoy code or assets were taken.
